'''Xile Hu''' (born 1978 in [[Putian]], [[China]]) is a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[chemist]] specialized in [[catalysis]]. He is a professor in chemistry at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and leads the Laboratory of Inorganic Synthesis and Catalysis at the School of Basic Sciences.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=LSCI |url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lsci/ |access-date=2020-11-23 |website=www.epfl.ch |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Career ==
Hu studied [[chemistry]] at [[Peking University]] and received his Bachelor’s degree in 2000. During his undergraduate, he worked with Jianhua Lin. He then joined the lab of [[Karsten Meyer (chemist)|Karsten Meyer]] at [[University of California, San Diego]] as [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD student]] and graduated with a thesis on "''Metal complexes of tripodal N-heterocyclic carbene ligands: synthesis, structure, bonding, and reactivity''."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Xile|first=Hu|date=|title=Metal Complexes of Tripodal N-Heterocyclic Carbene Ligands: Synthesis, Structure, Bonding, and Reactivity|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lsci/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/HuThesis.pdf|access-date=|website=}}</ref> In 2005, he went to work as [[postdoctoral researcher]] with [[Jonas C. Peters]] at the [[California Institute of Technology]]. Here he initiated and developed a research project on molecular electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hu|first1=Xile|last2=Brunschwig|first2=Bruce S.|last3=Peters|first3=Jonas C.|date=2007-07-01|title=Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution at Low Overpotentials by Cobalt Macrocyclic Glyoxime and Tetraimine Complexes|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja067876b|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=129|issue=29|pages=8988–8998|doi=10.1021/ja067876b|pmid=17602556|issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2007, he became [[Assistant professor|tenure-track Assistant Professor]] of chemistry at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]. In 2013, he was promoted as Associate Professor, and in 2016, he became Full Professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]. Since 2007 he has led the Laboratory of Inorganic Synthesis and Catalysis at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]'s School of Basic Sciences.<ref name=":1" /> In 2023 he co-founded a startup [https://www.novamea.swiss NovaMea], commercializing membranes, catalysts, and technologies for [[Anion exchange membrane electrolysis|anion exchange membrane]] (AEM) water electrolysis.

== Research ==
Hu's research group directs an [[Interdisciplinarity|interdisciplinary research]] program to develop chemistry that has a potential societal impact, for example, more sustainable and efficient methods to make bio-active compounds, non-precious electrocatalysts and fluorine-free membranes for renewable energy conversion and storage, or improved electrochemical devices.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Research|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/lsci/research/|access-date=2020-11-26|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> Their research cover many aspects of inorganic, organic, bio, applied physical, and electrochemistry, as well as chemical engineering. == Distinctions ==
In 2011, Hu won the Werner prize of the Swiss Chemical Society. In 2012 he was selected as an extraordinary young scientist by the [[World Economic Forum|world economic forum]]. In 2013, he received the ''Chemical Society Reviews'' Emerging Investigator Lectureship. In 2014, he won the [[European Medal for Bio-Inorganic Chemistry]] at the Eurobic conference. In 2015, he received the Young Researcher Award from the European Federation of Catalysis Societies. In 2016, he received the Bau Family Award in Inorganic Chemistry. In 2017, he was awarded with the [[Swiss Science Prize Latsis|National Latsis Prize]] by the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] and the [[Latsis Foundation|International Latsis Foundation]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=National Latsis Prize 2017 awarded to chemist Xile Hu - SNF|url=http://www.snf.ch/en/researchinFocus/newsroom/Pages/news-180116-national-latsis-prize-2017-awarded-to-xile-hu.aspx|access-date=2020-11-26|website=www.snf.ch}}</ref> the [[Organic Letters]] Outstanding Publication of the Year Lectureship for 2017,<ref name=":0" /> and the Tajima Prize by the [[International Society of Electrochemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Society of Electrochemistry|url=https://www.ise-online.org/awards/taj.php|access-date=2021-04-23|website=www.ise-online.org}}</ref> In 2018, he received the Resonate Award from Caltech,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Resonate Awards 2018|url=http://resnick.sites.caltech.edu/programs/past-programs/resonate-awards/resonate-awards-2018|access-date=2020-11-26|website=Resnick Sustainability Institute|language=en}}</ref> in 2019, the Homogeneous Catalysis Award by Royal Society of Chemistry,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Homogeneous Catalysis Award|url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/archives/homogeneous-catalysis-award/|access-date=2020-11-26|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|language=en-GB}}</ref> and in 2020, the International Catalysis Award by the International Association of Catalysis Societies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=17th International Congress in Catalysis {{!}} June 14–19, 2020 • San Diego, CA USA|url=https://2020icc.com/|access-date=2020-11-26|website=2020icc.com}}</ref> In 2022 he received Swiss Green & Sustainable Chemistry Award. In 2023 he received Robert K. Grasselli Award for Catalysis (European Federation of Catalysis Societies), and IUPAC-Zhejiang NH International Award for Green Chemistry Experienced Chemist Award. Hu has been named "Highly Cited Researcher" by [[Publons]] ([[Clarivate|Clarivate Analytics]]) every year from 2017 to current.<ref>{{Cite web|title=xile hu's Publons profile|url=https://publons.com/researcher/2847042/xile-hu/|access-date=2020-11-26|website=publons.com|language=en}}</ref>

In 2014, he became a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (UK), and in 2019 fellow of the [[European Academy of Sciences and Arts|European Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=European Academy of Sciences - Xile Hu |url=https://www.eurasc.eu/members/xile-huepfl-ch/member/ |access-date=2020-11-26 |website=www.eurasc.org }}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Since 2020 he is a member of the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Academy of Europe: Hu Xile|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Hu_Xile|access-date=2020-11-26|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>
